# V4.1 partner agreement publication workflow (Operation EMPOWER B2.10)

**Status:** ready to run. It is waiting for the founders to supply the approved V4.1 agreement document. No agreement text is in this repository, and none was written or generated by this operation.

The workflow publishes the supplied document **byte for byte**. The founders can prove it is unchanged at every stage: importer, published page, and each partner's acceptance record.

## What the platform already enforces

- An agreement is content of kind `agreement`. It is partner-only, has a 3-month review cadence, has no structured fields and must contain its full text (at least 200 characters).
- Each version must cite its legal review as a source beginning `legal:`.
- **Two founders:** the author cannot approve their own agreement while another founder is active.
- A published version can never be edited, only superseded.
- **Fingerprint:** `partner_agreement_digest(title, body)` is the SHA-256 of the title, a blank line, then the body, encoded as UTF-8. It is shown on the activation page and the agreement page, and stored on every acceptance.
- **Invitations:** a founder can issue one only for a published, current agreement version. Activation records acceptance of exactly that version, and a database trigger refuses activation without it.
- **Batching:** agreements are never part of a batch review action (`empower-content-batch.ts` refuses them).

## Steps

### 1. Receive the documents

Receive the final, solicitor-reviewed V4.1 agreement as Markdown or plain text (no HTML), with its exact title and the legal review reference.

### 2. Fingerprint the file

Do this before importing (no database access):

```bash
cd admin
node scripts/agreement-fingerprint.mjs --file=<agreement.md> --title="<exact title>"
```

Record the 64-character fingerprint, and confirm it with the person who supplied the document.

### 3. Dry run the import

```bash
node scripts/import-partner-agreement.mjs --file=<agreement.md> --title="<exact title>" --legal-ref=legal:<review-ref> --dry-run
```

It must print the same fingerprint as step 2.

### 4. Import as a draft

This needs founder approval for the target database:

```bash
AGREEMENT_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL=<provisioning URL> node scripts/import-partner-agreement.mjs --file=<agreement.md> --title="<exact title>" \
  --legal-ref=legal:<review-ref> --founder-email=<author founder> --allow-database=<production database name> --confirm-import
```

The importer:
- refuses non-test databases unless `--allow-database` names the target
- refuses HTML or a short file
- refuses if a version of the agreement is already in progress
- re-reads the stored text and confirms the database fingerprint matches before committing
- writes an `empower_agreement_imported` audit entry

### 5. Submit the draft

The author founder opens **Founder workspace → Content**, finds the `independent-partner-agreement` draft, previews it and submits it.

### 6. Approve

The **second founder** reads the full text and approves it, with the legal review reference and a review-by date no more than 3 months ahead.

### 7. Publish and verify

Either founder publishes it. Then confirm:
- the fingerprint on the published version equals the step 2 value;
- `partner_agreement_current(<version id>)` is true.

### 8. Issue invitations

Only now set `PARTNER_ACTIVATION_ENABLED=true` (see [PRODUCTION-FEATURE-MATRIX.md](PRODUCTION-FEATURE-MATRIX.md)), then issue invitations from the Recruitment tab.

### 9. Verify with a synthetic applicant

Use a founder-owned mailbox for a test invitation. The activation page must show the same fingerprint before acceptance.

## Verification evidence

- The importer and fingerprint tool were exercised against the disposable browser database with a fixture labelled TEST ONLY. The fixture is not contractual wording and is not committed. See [evidence/b2-10/README.md](evidence/b2-10/README.md).
- The invitation, acceptance and activation path is covered by `partner-invitations.database.test.ts`, `partner-onboarding.integration.test.ts` and the `partner-onboarding.spec.ts` browser journey, all of which pass.

## Not to do

- Do not publish a draft whose filename resembles an approved agreement.
- Do not paste the agreement by hand.
- Do not approve your own agreement version.
- Do not enable activation before step 7.
